newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says no Northwest result in Q4.
newsitem.headline: KLM says no Northwest result in Q4.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday that its fourth quarter net earnings would not include any result from its stake in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines.
"The forecast net result for the fourth quarter contains no result from KLM's stake in Northwest Airlines," KLM said in a results statement.

KLM owns an 18.8 percent stake in Northwest. The U.S. airline returned to positive equity in December, which entitles KLM to book its share of Northwest profits in its final 1996/97 quarter ending March 31.
In the fourth quarter of 1995/96, KLM's revaluation of its preference shares in Northwest amounted to 92 million guilders.

"KLM has repeatedly stated that it expected to book its share of Northwest profits during the course of 1997...we did not say when," spokesman Hans Leijte said, adding that to date Northwest had given no official notification of its return to positive shareholders' equity.
As such the fourth quarter result from Northwest would comprise the interest on KLM's preferred shareholdings. In the current quarter ended December 31, 1996, this amounted to three milion guilders.
KLM said the Focus 2000 programme, announced in November at the presentation of its half-year results, had identified major improvement projects.
"Most projects are defined, project managers appointed and financial goals set," it said.
Unions and works councils would need to be consulted on new projects, it added.
Projects already being implemented included the development of a new revenue management system, electronic shopping and the introduction of a new sales and distribution approach.
KLM said similar projects had been started in the cargo division, where it was introducing new information technology to further improve capacity utilisation.
"Enhanced joint purchasing as well as further realization of synergies with our partners are also part of Focus 2000," KLM added.
